newsitem.title: POLAND: ZLOTY JUST UP VS BASKET DESPITE DLR SHORT-COVERING.
newsitem.headline: ZLOTY JUST UP VS BASKET DESPITE DLR SHORT-COVERING.

text.p: The bullish Polish zloty firmed only slightly against the parity rate as domestic short currency position covering partly offset the supply of currencies coming from abroad, dealers said.

They said banks were closing short positions after recent central bank interventions taking advantage of the dollar's world strength and slower foreign activity on the secondary treasuries market, heavily drained by high-yield hunters.
"The recent five-figure zloty nose-dive sparked some domestic stop-loss currency buying, which partly offset currency inflows," said Maciej Grabosz from Bank Zachodni SA.

The zloty closed at 3.18/3.13 percent from the parity rate, slightly stronger than Wednesday's close at 3.13/3.00 percent. It closed at 2.9710/25 to the dollar, down from 2.9650/00 on Wednesday and at 1.8100/10 to the mark, down from 1.8075/00.

Players expected slower trade on Friday as the market was reeling from the recent wave of foreign inflows estimated at about $350 million and the Monday and Wednesday NBP interventions totalling some $100 million.
"After wave of foreign investment and zloty rate swings nobody is likely to keep big positions open in the coming days," said a forex dealer at a Polish bank.
Some dealers said there was increased supply of half-year T-bills on the secondary market as domestic players switched to higher yielding 182-day NBP-bills.
The NBP sold 156.5 million zlotys worth of half-year paper at an average yield 0.01 point up at 22.00 percent, today.
Half-year T-bills were quoted at 20.10/19.90 percent on the secondary market against the last primary average yield of 26-week T-bills at 19.73 percent.
The central bank also drained a total of 514 million zlotys for six days at a flat maximum rate of 21.63 percent and for 14 days at an unchanged 21.64 percent.
Overnight rates were quoted flat at 21.30/21.50 percent, tomorrow/next were 0.05 point down at 21.35/21.55 percent.
